notes: Third post-review fix, reported directly by a student-facing screenshot: illogical line breaks splitting a coefficient from its power of ten (e.g. '6.02 ×' ending one line, '10²³' starting the next) and, more generally, a number splitting from its unit. Root cause was two-fold in the scratchpad latex.py converter: (1) LaTeX's ~ (e.g. \mathrm{~N}) was being converted to an ordinary breakable space instead of a non-breaking one - wrong on ~'s own LaTeX semantics, not just a style choice; (2) the multiplication/dot/division signs had ordinary spaces on both sides with nothing stopping the browser wrapping right after the operator. Fixed both: ~ now emits an actual non-breaking space; a final whitespace-cleanup pass wraps the spaces immediately around ×/·/÷ in non-breaking spaces too, and collapses any run of an ordinary space touching a non-breaking one down to a single non-breaking space (so a literal source space next to a ~-derived one never doubles up into a visibly wider gap). notes: Eighth post-review request: a literal '/' typed directly in source (not \frac{}{}) should render as a proper stacked fraction like \frac does, not a bare slash - this chapter writes divisions this way constantly. Implemented by rewriting a bare '/' into \frac{num}{den} syntax before the main converter runs, so the existing \frac handling renders it (rather than a second fraction-rendering implementation). Four real bugs caught and fixed while getting the numerator/denominator boundary detection right, each verified against actual chapter content, not just synthetic examples: (1) a '(A/B)' fully wrapped in one paren becomes the fraction directly, dropping the redundant parens (regex pass first); (2) remaining '/' only counts at bracket-depth 0, with the numerator/denominator each extending to the nearest depth-0 '=' or '\times'/'×' - so a chain like 'A/B × C/D' splits into two fractions around the ×, not one swallowing everything; (3) a '\times' gluing a coefficient to its own power of ten (2.3 \times 10^-8) must never count as that boundary, or the search stops right there and drops the coefficient - caught on ex_1.3b/ex_1.7's acceleration calculations, where '2.3×10⁻⁸ N / 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg' was coming out as '10⁻⁸ N / 9.11' before the fix; (4) '\text{...}' (trailing prose inside a math span, e.g. 'है।') must also be a boundary, or the denominator search runs past the actual math and swallows the prose whole - caught on the same ex_1.3b passage ('s² है।' collapsing into one fraction denominator before the fix). Separately, a '/' inside a superscript exponent (x^{1/2}, a fractional power) must stay a compact superscript, never get promoted to a full stacked fraction crammed inside a <sup> tag - caught on ex_1.10/ex_1.11's alpha*x^(1/2) field expressions; fixed by having the superscript handler's fallback path bypass the division-rewrite for its own content entirely (the exponent's protective braces are already gone by the time that content is a standalone string, so depth-tracking alone can't distinguish it from ordinary text anymore). Regenerated 09_design/final.hi.html and 10_pdf/final.hi.pdf, re-ran all checks (clean), visually re-confirmed on the exact reported item (ex_1.3b) and the fractional-exponent edge case (ex_1.10/ex_1.11) that both render correctly. Page count grew 28->30 (more vertical space per stacked fraction than inline text needed) - expected and acceptable. All four bug classes documented at length in step_9/PROMPT.md.

notes: Ninth post-review fix, reported directly (ex_1.3b's acceleration computation 'a = 2.3e-8 N/9.11e-31 kg = 2.5e22 m/s^2' splitting unevenly across two lines - the first '= fraction' stayed intact but the second one still fell to its own line, half the equation above and half below). Root cause: the non-breaking-space padding already added around '=' only prevents a break AT THAT SPACE CHARACTER - it does not stop the browser choosing a different break point at the boundary between plain text and an adjacent inline-block-like element (a fraction's .s31 span), so nothing was stopping a wrap immediately BEFORE the second '='. Fixed by rendering a \frac/\sqrt that immediately follows '=' right there and gluing both inside one more .s90 nowrap span - and critically, chaining through every further '= <frac/sqrt>' that follows immediately into the SAME span, not gluing each '=' independently (gluing only one at a time left the later ones free to wrap apart from each other, exactly as broken-looking as the original problem). Verified in isolation first (test script) before touching the real page. Regenerated 09_design/final.hi.html and 10_pdf/final.hi.pdf, re-ran all checks (clean), visually re-confirmed on the exact reported line that the whole equation now moves together to its own line as one unit. Documented in step_9/PROMPT.md alongside the other '=' and division fixes.
